Position Overview

Mills-Peninsula Medical Center, a not-for-profit corporation with 2,496 employees, operates two community health facilities with a total of 301 inpatient beds.

The Chief Executive Officer (CEO), Mills Peninsula Medical Center (MPMC) directs and facilitates operations throughout the acute care campus and aligns MPMC strategy with Sutter Health strategic plans. The CEO assures integration among medical staff, nursing, clinical and support services professionals to achieve optimal patient care and internal services excellence. The CEO provides leadership direction and administration of operations to ensure compliance with current established policies and strategic objectives while supporting the realization of Sutter’s future objectives. Assures quality of care and cost-effective services are provided to the community. Exercises necessary, appropriate authority and accountability for the operations and long-range planning for the Entity's and other associated health services business entities. Maintains effective employee, medical staff and community and Entity Board relations. Promotes positive community contacts and relationships. Serves as the operational liaison between medical staff leadership, MPMC Board members and Entity and system leaders. Reporting directly to the Division President, the CEO will work in collaboration with the CME and CNE and other senior MPMC leaders, as well as serve as a member of the Sutter Division Leadership Team. This position is accountable for oversight of the quality of care, cost effective services, and exercises necessary and appropriate authority and accountability for all MPMC departments. The CEO works collaboratively with Foundation Administrators and other Division leadership to develop integrated approaches to service area growth and development.

The CEO is also responsible for directing patient care efforts through the Entity's senior leadership team to guide managers and supervisors of the individual entities within the acute care Entities and service lines. The position has overall responsibility for the managers and supervisors’ development and implementation of plan(s) for the MPMC staffing, program development, directing and monitoring MPMC operations, quality improvement programs and sound fiscal management of the departments. The CEO may also have responsibility for outpatient and ambulatory operations, including but not limited to, clinics, urgent care centers, surgery centers, specialty care, same-day/walk-ins, clinical service lines and support and shared services. The CEO sets the tone and processes for a culture that rewards leadership, teamwork, innovation, and accountability, and promotes productive collaboration among senior team members, departments, and all other management levels.

Help more people say "yes" to changing lives.

This isn't a role where you'll inherit a large fundraising department and simply keep everything running.

This is an opportunity to help shape the future of an organization with a strong reputation, an engaged Board of Directors, healthy financial reserves, and tremendous room for growth.
You'll work directly alongside our CEO to build the next generation of fundraising at International Relief Teams.

Together, you'll strengthen relationships with current supporters, cultivate new major donors, expand corporate partnerships, grow foundation funding, elevate our community presence, and inspire more people to become part of our mission.

If you've ever wanted the opportunity to leave your fingerprint on an organization—not just manage one—this is that opportunity.

About International Relief Teams

International Relief Teams is a humanitarian nonprofit organization dedicated to improving lives by providing life’s essentials of food, water, shelter, and medicine.
Around the world, our programs help people recover from disasters, access food and life-saving medicines, and build healthier futures.
Closer to home, we mobilize volunteers to pack meals for families facing food insecurity, build homes in Tijuana, respond to disasters, and create meaningful opportunities for people to serve their communities.
Since our founding in 1988, we've:
Delivered more than $770 million
in humanitarian aid
Served people in 78 countries

Mobilized more than 7,500 volunteers

Behind every humanitarian program is a team of people making sure the details are handled with excellence.
That's where you come in.

What You'll Do

Lead Our Fundraising Strategy

Develop and execute a comprehensive fundraising strategy aligned with International Relief Teams' strategic plan and long-term vision.
Diversify revenue through annual giving, monthly giving, major gifts, foundations, corporations, grants, planned giving, signature fundraising events, and other philanthropic partnerships.
Develop and manage the annual development budget and regularly evaluate fundraising performance against established goals.
Identify new fundraising opportunities and implement innovative strategies that expand philanthropic support and strengthen long-term sustainability.
Establish measurable goals and key performance indicators (KPIs), using fundraising metrics, technology, and data to guide strategy and improve results.
Prepare fundraising reports, dashboards, and strategic recommendations for the CEO and Board of Directors, and present progress toward fundraising goals at Board and committee meetings.

Build Meaningful Donor Relationships

Personally manage a portfolio of major donors and prospective supporters.
Identify, cultivate, solicit, and steward transformational gifts.
Partner closely with the CEO on donor strategy, relationship management, and major gift solicitations.
Develop thoughtful stewardship experiences that deepen donor engagement and inspire long-term support.
Ensure timely, meaningful gift acknowledgments and donor communications that reflect the organization's commitment to gratitude and relationship-building.

Grow Strategic Partnerships

Build and strengthen relationships with corporations, foundations, civic leaders, nonprofit partners, and community organizations.
Identify partnership opportunities that increase both philanthropic support and awareness of International Relief Teams' mission.
Represent International Relief Teams at community meetings, networking events, conferences, and donor gatherings.
Serve as the primary development liaison to the Board of Directors, helping equip and inspire Board members to become confident ambassadors and fundraising partners.

Lead Grant & Institutional Giving

Oversee the organization's grant strategy, including identifying funding opportunities, developing competitive proposals, coordinating supporting materials, and ensuring timely reporting.
Collaborate with program staff, consultants, and partners to develop compelling grant applications and communicate program impact to institutional funders.
Build and maintain strong relationships with foundation, corporate, and government funding partners.

Create Exceptional Fundraising Events

Lead the planning, execution, and evaluation of the organization's signature fundraising event(s), ensuring every detail contributes to an outstanding guest experience and meaningful fundraising results.
Develop event budgets, timelines, sponsorship strategies, volunteer committees, vendor relationships, and logistics to deliver successful fundraising events from start to finish.
Partner with the CEO, staff, Board of Directors, volunteers, and event vendors to create memorable experiences that strengthen donor relationships, inspire generosity, and elevate the International Relief Teams brand.
Measure event performance, analyze return on investment, and continually improve future fundraising events based on results and participant feedback.

Strengthen Our Fundraising Systems

Partner with the Development Data Associate to leverage Raiser's Edge as a strategic fundraising tool, ensuring accurate donor information, meaningful stewardship, effective prospect management, and insightful reporting.
Develop and improve fundraising systems, policies, and procedures that support moves management, stewardship, gift acknowledgments, prospect tracking, and reporting.
Leverage fundraising technology and analytics to improve decision-making, donor engagement, and operational efficiency.
Manage outside fundraising consultants, grant writers, event professionals, and other partners as needed to strengthen fundraising efforts.

Inspire Others

Supervise, mentor, and develop members of the development team, fostering a culture of collaboration, accountability, innovation, and continuous improvement.
Partner with the CEO and leadership team to cultivate an organization-wide culture where philanthropy is understood as a shared responsibility.
Support and encourage Board members, volunteers, and staff in meaningful donor engagement and fundraising activities.
Serve as a visible champion for International Relief Teams' mission, values, and commitment to compassionate humanitarian service.

WHO YOU ARE

We're less interested in checking every box than finding the right person.
The strongest candidates will likely bring many of the following:
A proven track record of securing major gifts and building meaningful donor relationships.
Experience creating and implementing fundraising strategy—not simply maintaining existing programs.
Confidence asking for philanthropic investments.
Strong relationship-building skills with donors, volunteers, executives, and Board members.
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills.
Experience managing fundraising databases such as Raiser's Edge.
The ability to think strategically while also rolling up your sleeves and getting things done.
A collaborative leadership style that brings out the best in others.
Genuine passion for humanitarian work and serving communities with dignity.

YOU'LL LOVE THIS JOB IF...

✔ You genuinely enjoy meeting people and building authentic relationships.
✔ You're energized by building something better than what existed before.
✔ You enjoy wearing multiple hats and solving new challenges.
✔ You like having direct access to your CEO and helping shape organizational strategy.
✔ You're excited by the opportunity to grow an already respected nonprofit into something even greater.

THIS JOB PROBABLY ISN'T FOR YOU IF...

You prefer maintaining existing systems rather than building new ones.
You dislike networking or asking for gifts.
You need highly structured environments where every process already exists.
You prefer working behind the scenes instead of representing an organization publicly.
You view fundraising primarily as grant writing or event planning.

COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

LOCATION

This is a full-time, onsite leadership position based at our headquarters in Mission Valley, San Diego.
Because collaboration, mentoring, and relationship-building are central to this role, regular in-office presence is important.

·        A cover letter telling us why this role interests you
·        Tell us about 1-2 fundraising projects you lead that you’re especially proud of. This could be a major gift, campaign, event, corporate partnership, grant, donor stewardship initiative, etc.

DIRECTOR OF DEVELOPMENT
Location: San Francisco Bay Area
Salary Range: $135,000–$165,000, commensurate with experience

ABOUT 826 NATIONAL
826 National is the largest youth writing network in the country. We amplify the impact of our network of youth writing and publishing centers and elevate the voices of young authors. We believe writing is far more than an academic skill—it is a tool for young people to ignite their creativity, explore identity, advocate for themselves and their communities, and shape their futures.

Together with nine chapters and 826 Digital, the 826 Network serves more than 950,000 students ages 6–18 each year. More than 50 organizations around the world have also adapted the 826 model, collectively serving an additional 150,000 young people annually.

We are working toward a future in which every young person has access to the power and joy of writing.

POSITION SUMMARY
826 National seeks an entrepreneurial, visionary Director of Development to lead the organization's next phase of fundraising growth.

Reporting to the CEO, this leader will develop and execute a bold national fundraising strategy, oversee an integrated development and communications team, cultivate transformational philanthropic partnerships, and help shape the future of one of the country's leading youth writing organizations.

This is an exciting opportunity for a relationship-driven fundraiser who enjoys building as much as sustaining—someone energized by identifying new opportunities, opening doors, and inspiring investment in innovative national initiatives. The Director of Development will partner closely with the CEO and Board of Directors to grow philanthropic support, strengthen a culture of philanthropy across the organization and network, and expand 826 National's visibility among leading funders in education, youth development, arts, literacy, and youth mental health.

The ideal candidate brings deep experience fundraising on a national stage, an established network of philanthropic relationships, and the strategic vision to expand 826 National's reach among leading institutional and individual funders.

Reports to
: CEO
Supervises
: Development Manager, Finance & Development Coordinator, Senior Communications Manager
Status
: Full-time

MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES

Strategic Leadership
Develop and lead a multi-year fundraising strategy that advances 826 National's next phase of organizational growth.
Partner closely with the CEO, Board of Directors, and leadership team to establish ambitious fundraising goals and strategies.
Lead the organization in growing contributed revenue while diversifying funding streams and strengthening long-term sustainability.
Design and implement strategies to grow annual revenue from approximately $3 million to $4 million through expanded philanthropic investment and innovative fundraising approaches.
Serve as a member of the leadership team, contributing to organizational strategy, culture, and long-term planning.
Evaluate and analyze the existing development program and implement effective changes, responses to a changing environment, and policies and procedures to increase overall fundraising performance

Fundraising & Relationship Management
Position 826 National as a premier national philanthropic investment by cultivating transformative relationships with leading foundations, corporations, and major individual donors across the United States, securing significant investments that fuel the organization's next phase of growth.
Envision and lead a nationwide fundraising strategy that leverages existing relationships while building new partnerships with nationally recognized foundations, corporate partners, and major individual philanthropists to advance 826 National's mission and growth. Envision and lead national fundraising initiatives and campaigns that elevate 826 National's mission and expand philanthropic support.
Manage a portfolio of major individual, foundation, and corporate donors, leading all cultivation, solicitation, stewardship, and relationship strategy.
Build and steward strong relationships with national foundations, corporations, major donors, and philanthropic leaders.
Partner with the CEO and Board members to cultivate transformational gifts, multi-year investments, and strategic partnerships.
Lead organization-wide moves management systems that deepen donor engagement and increase philanthropic investment.

Communications & External Engagement
Provide strategic leadership for fundraising communications, ensuring all messaging compellingly communicates organizational impact and inspires investment.
Oversee the development of grant proposals, reports, campaign materials, project budgets, the annual report, and other fundraising communications.
Guide organizational communications strategy, including donor communications, newsletters, social media, media opportunities, conference strategy, and mission storytelling in partnership with the communications team.
Serve as an engaging spokesperson for 826 National with funders, partners, conferences, and national audiences.

Team & Network Leadership
Lead, mentor, and develop a high-performing Development and Communications team grounded in collaboration, accountability, continuous learning, and shared success.
Foster a strong culture of philanthropy across 826 National.
Partner with Executive Directors and development leaders across the 826 Network to identify and pursue collaborative fundraising opportunities and strengthen fundraising capacity nationwide.
Steward a national community of Chapter development leaders.
Lead planning and execution of fundraising events, donor experiences, and cultivation opportunities.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS
Bachelor's degree or equivalent professional experience.
A genuine passion for 826 National's mission and belief in the transformative power of writing.
At least 10 years of progressive responsibility experience in fundraising.
At least 5 years of experience leading and developing fundraising teams.
Demonstrated success leading fundraising for a national or multi-regional nonprofit organization.
Proven track record of raising significant philanthropic revenue for a national or multi-regional organization, including developing and executing a national fundraising strategy. Demonstrated success cultivating and stewarding relationships with national foundations, corporations, and major individual donors, with an established network of philanthropic relationships across the United States.
Proven experience securing six- and seven-figure gifts from individuals, foundations, and corporations.
Experience fundraising within a national philanthropic landscape, with strong understanding of—and ideally existing relationships within—national foundation, corporate, and major donor communities.
Demonstrated success developing and executing fundraising strategies that result in significant revenue growth.
Exceptional relationship-building skills with donors, volunteers, board members, and organizational leaders.
Experience partnering closely with boards of directors and executive leadership.
Outstanding written and verbal communication skills, with exceptional storytelling ability.
Strong strategic thinking, organizational leadership, and project management skills.
Extensive experience with Salesforce or comparable CRM platforms.
A collaborative leadership style that builds trust across teams and functions.
Demonstrated commitment to thoughtful donor stewardship and authentic relationship building.
A proactive, entrepreneurial mindset with enthusiasm for networking, face-to-face relationship building, and identifying new opportunities.
826 National imagines applicants with backgrounds in cause marketing, corporate and foundation relations, and sponsorship, sales, and frontline fundraising to be particularly applicable.

ABOUT THE TEAM
Based primarily in San Francisco, the 826 National team is a collaborative group of passionate professionals dedicated to championing young writers, advancing writing education nationally, and supporting the work of the 826 Network and 826 Digital.

Our work is grounded in five organizational values:
Power & Potential of Youth: We believe in the power of young voices, the possibility in their ideas, and the value of their words.
Commitment to Creativity & Learning: We foster creativity and lifelong learning through high-quality, evidence-based experiences.
The Transformative Power of Writing: We believe writing unlocks confidence, agency, and opportunity.
Strength of Community: We believe lasting impact is created through collaboration and collective action.
Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Belonging: We strive to embed these principles throughout our culture, programs, and partnerships.

BENEFITS
826 National offers a comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental, vision, retirement benefits, paid holidays, and 15 days of paid vacation during the first two years of employment, with additional vacation accrual thereafter.

Please visit https://826national.typeform.com/to/XPyMmlu6
to submit your resume and a thoughtful cover letter describing your interest in the role and your relevant experience.

jobs.description:
Job Description

We believe in bold ideas, diverse perspectives, and the drive to transform knowledge into impact. Here, your curiosity fuels progress, your voice shapes innovation, and your ambition helps redefine what’s possible within science and learning. We are a culture that obsesses over impact, challenges, and drives what’s next to power infinite possibilities for our customers, colleagues and society at large.

About The Role

The Chief of Staff to the CEO is one of the most consequential and demanding roles in the organization and one of the most distinct. This is not a traditional leadership role with a defined team, a clear mandate, or visible deliverables. It is a role built on influence without authority, on making others more effective rather than being visibly effective yourself, and on operating with the full trust of the CEO in a highly matrixed, fast-moving environment. The ideal candidate is a high-potential leader who is intellectually curious, politically astute, and genuinely energized by the challenge of working through others to drive outcomes that matter at the enterprise level.

Key Responsibilities

Coordination and Administration

Assist in managing the CEO’s agenda, ensuring focus on highest-priority areas.
Develop agendas for CEO-led meetings: ELT meetings, quarterly meetings, off-sites, etc. Work with CEO to identify key themes and topics and solicit input as needed from key stakeholders. Disseminate information to participants and coordinate follow-up.
Coordinate other CEO-led events and activities. Assist in developing content and agenda.
Coordinate board preparation; develop and disseminate materials; involve key stakeholders (among the ELT and others) as needed.
Ensure all materials shared with the CEO are synthesized, accurate, and current — always go to the source owners to verify information before distributing. Avoid relying on prior or undated materials.

Strategic Project Management

Lead and manage high-priority strategic initiatives on behalf of the CEO and executive leadership team, serving as project sponsor or direct project lead as appropriate.
Drive cross-functional strategic projects that span multiple business units, ensuring alignment with corporate objectives and timely delivery of outcomes.
Support the ELT in annual and multi-year strategic planning processes, including facilitating planning sessions, coordinating input from business units, and synthesizing strategic recommendations.
Identify and address critical organizational challenges that require CEO-level attention, developing action plans and mobilizing resources to drive resolution.
Track progress on enterprise-wide strategic initiatives; create executive dashboards and provide regular updates to the CEO and ELT on milestone achievements and risk mitigation.
Partner with business unit leaders to accelerate transformation initiatives, remove roadblocks, and ensure strategic alignment across the organization.
Conduct deep-dive analyses on strategic opportunities — including market entry, partnerships, M&A targets, or new business models — preparing executive-ready recommendations.
Serve as the CEO’s representative on select strategic workstreams, committees, or task forces, ensuring CEO priorities are reflected and progress is maintained.
A note on operating mode:
The Chief of Staff role is most powerful when it works – and wins – through others. Unlike a project owner with direct authority, this role operates through influence, facilitation, and relationship. The instinct to drive and own outcomes must be balanced with the discipline to let others lead — surfacing their thinking, giving them credit, and sequencing decisions so they land at the right moment, through the right voice.

Research

Coordinate background material and arrange briefings with CEO on important external meetings (investors, strategic hires, industry figures, etc.), working with Investor Relations, Business Heads, HR, and Corporate Communications.
Identify internal and external trends and events the CEO should be aware of, and prepare or coordinate background material as appropriate.
Ensure all information provided to the CEO is synthesized and summarized in a way that is accurate, reliable, and easy to consume — go directly to source owners to verify currency and correctness.

Relationship-Building

Maintain ongoing, positive relationships with all ELT members and other important stakeholders.
Ensure that the chief of staff role is apolitical — exercise judgment and discretion in disseminating information. Exercise confidentiality regarding privileged information.
Be seen as helpful and collaborative at all times; avoid assuming an unhelpful gatekeeper role.
Invest heavily in building relationship capital before it is needed. Early time spent in genuine, non-transactional engagement with ELT members pays dividends when influence is required later. Logic without relationship gets nowhere in a peer-influence environment.
Be explicit and disciplined about which mode you are operating in when engaging with senior executives: acting on the CEO’s behalf, offering your own perspective, or facilitating. Conflating these modes creates confusion and erodes trust.
Practice active listening as a core competency. When receiving feedback that differs from your perspective, pause, ask clarifying questions, and seek to understand before responding. Curiosity and openness are professional strengths in this role.

Advisory

Provide counsel to the CEO on critical business decisions and organizational challenges.
Feed organizational intelligence back to the CEO as appropriate.
Develop strong judgment about what to escalate vs. what to handle or redirect. Calibrate this explicitly and continuously with the CEO. Escalating too much reduces your value-add; escalating too little risks overstepping authority. Ask regularly: “Would you have wanted to know about X?”
Internalize that the “right” answer delivered at the wrong time, through the wrong messenger, or in the wrong room often produces a worse outcome than a less-optimal answer delivered well. Timing and sequencing are part of the answer.

What Success Looks Like In This Role

Many of the Chief of Staff’s most important contributions are invisible by design. A meeting that runs well because it was set up properly, a brewing conflict that dissolves before it reaches the CEO, a stalled decision that moves forward — these are the real deliverables. Success in this role is often measured by what didn’t happen, not by artifacts produced or decisions owned.

Indicators Of Strong Performance

Executives feel better prepared, aligned, and supported — and attribute that to themselves and their teams, not to the CoS.
The CEO’s time is protected and consistently applied to the highest-priority areas.
Information reaching the CEO is accurate, synthesized, and timely.
Cross-functional initiatives move forward without bottlenecks; the CoS is seen as a connector and enabler, not a checkpoint.
Trust with the ELT is high; the CoS is sought out, not worked around.

Qualifications

Ability to work closely with C-level executives; demonstrated professionalism, integrity, sense of urgency, discretion, and superior organizational skills.
Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment with appropriate technology fluency.
Outstanding communication skills, both written and verbal.
High emotional intelligence and ability to navigate sensitive situations with discretion.
Capacity to listen deeply and learn continuously — this role rewards pattern recognition developed through observation more than frameworks delivered through presentation.
Resilient and composed under pressure; able to stay grounded during an extended adjustment period (the transition into this role typically takes six to nine months before someone feels fully competent).
Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities with the ability to structure ambiguous problems and drive to actionable solutions.
Experience with project management methodologies and tools; ability to manage complex, multi-stakeholder initiatives.
Strategic thinking capability with the ability to connect tactical activities to broader organizational objectives.
Genuine commitment to professional networking — internally and externally — as a core working discipline, not an afterthought. Peer CoS relationships (within and outside the company) are a professional asset and a necessary sounding board for navigating this uniquely demanding role.

Additional Notes

The role requires flexibility, including occasional evening and weekend work. Some travel will be required.

For more than 200 years, we've transformed knowledge into discoveries that shape the world. Today, our global team of innovators, creators, and experts is driving what's next in science, education, and publishing—creating impact that reaches everywhere.

We're not just observers of progress. We're the ones accelerating scientific breakthroughs, advancing learning, and sparking innovation that redefines entire fields and improves lives.

THE SALVATION ARMY

NORTH & CENTRAL ILLINOIS DIVISION

Job Description

JOB TITLE:
Deputy Director of Social Services

PEOPLE MANAGER:
(Yes/No) Yes

REPORTS TO:
Executive Director of Social Services

FLSA STATUS:
Exempt

PAY GRADE:
413

PAY RANGE:
$139,450 - $174,312

Who We Are

At The Salvation Army, we are dedicated to “Doing the Most Good”. We are made up of thousands of officers, soldiers, staff, volunteers, donors, and partners working together to holistically meet the physical, emotional, and spiritual needs of our most vulnerable neighbors. We do this through programs designed to combat homelessness and hunger, provide safe spaces for kids after school and on the weekends, achieve and maintain sobriety, and give hope to the hopeless. The Salvation Army North and Central Illinois Division provides these services to people in need.

Job Summary

The Deputy Director of Social Services serves as the second-in-command of the Social Services Department, working in close partnership with the Executive Director of Social Services to provide divisional leadership, continuity, and accountability across the department. The Deputy Director helps advance department-wide strategy, planning, and priorities across all department capacities – Program Operations; Mission Investment Management; and Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning. In addition, the Deputy Director provides direct supervision to the three Regional Directors of Social Services serving Northwest Illinois, Central Illinois, and Chicago, ensuring consistent program oversight and site support across a large, geographically diverse Division by holding Regional Directors accountable for program quality, compliance, community engagement, and staff development within their regions.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Areas of responsibility include but are not limited to the following:

Divisional Deputy Leadership

Serves as second-in-command to the Executive Director of Social Services, acting on the Executive Director’s behalf and exercising delegated authority in their absence to ensure continuity of divisional leadership and decision-making.
Partners with the Executive Director on divisional strategy, planning, and department-wide priorities, and supports the setting of direction across all department capacities.
Represents the Executive Director and Social Services Department in internal and external settings as delegated, including with divisional leadership, funders, community partners, and committees.
Supports coordination and alignment across the divisional Senior Directors of Program Operations; Mission Investment Management; and Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning to advance shared department objectives.
Contributes to the development of departmental policies, procedures, and processes, and supports their consistent implementation across the department.

Regional Oversight and Divisional Authority

Provides oversight of social services delivery across the Division's three geographic regions – Northwest Illinois, Central Illinois, and Chicago – ensuring Regional Directors connect program sites to Program Operations support, Mission Investment Management, and Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning.
Provides direct supervision to the Regional Directors of Social Services, holding each accountable for the effectiveness of their regional team and the quality of support delivered to program sites.
Establishes and maintains the standards, expectations, and accountability structures that guide Regional Directors in delivering consistent, high-quality support across their regions.
Ensures clear role clarity across regional teams, resolving escalation questions as they arise and facilitating effective matrix relationships between Regional Directors and the divisional functional heads of Program Operations, Mission Investment Management, and Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning.
Coordinates with the Senior Directors of Program Operations, Mission Investment Management, and Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning to ensure regional counterparts are effectively connected to divisional resources, standards, and tools.
Anticipates and responds to changes in the regional operating environment and ensures Regional Directors are positioned to adapt their teams accordingly.

Impact Area Stewardship and Field Connectivity

Ensures Regional Directors serve as effective partners with site advisory boards, providing strategic guidance on program planning and community-responsive program development within their impact areas.
Ensures every active program site in each region has a clear and accessible regional point of contact for administrative support, program development, and capacity building.
Monitors the effectiveness of Regional Directors and their teams across all three geographic regions for consistency, responsiveness, and quality of site support.
Identifies patterns of field need across regions, ensures regional teams have what they need to support sites effectively, and escalates systemic issues to the Executive Director of Social Services.

Community Representation and Stakeholder Partnership

Ensures Regional Directors represent The Salvation Army effectively at regional and local levels, connecting program sites to community service agencies, social service providers, governmental agencies, and funding sources.
Supports Regional Directors in building and sustaining local stakeholder relationships that advance mission outcomes and increase community visibility for program sites.
Coordinates with corps officers, program and related institution directors, and local advisory boards, through Regional Directors, to advance program development that is grounded in community need and aligned with divisional priorities.
Represents The Salvation Army on regional and local committees, task forces, and community planning bodies, as assigned.
Cooperates with other social service agencies in community planning, needs assessments, information and referral, and case management coordination, as appropriate.

Regional Program Oversight Coordination

Oversee Regional Directors’ work to ensure program sites within each region maintain compliance with licensing, accreditation, and Salvation Army standards.
Coordinates with the Senior Director of Mission Investment Management to ensure compliance support reaches program sites effectively through the matrix.
Supports Regional Directors in conducting periodic program reviews that assess service quality, fiscal alignment, and consistency with divisional priorities.
Coordinates with the Senior Director of Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning to ensure outcome tools and performance tracking support reaches program sites effectively through the matrix.
Ensures that program development proposals or modifications at the regional and site level reflect community need, divisional strategic priorities, and organizational capacity before advancing to the Executive Director.

Capacity Building and Staff Development

Builds the leadership capacity of Regional Directors through direct supervision, mentorship, and ongoing professional development, ensuring each director has the skills to lead their regional team effectively.
Ensures Regional Directors equip their site-level teams with the knowledge, tools, and practical support needed to deliver programs effectively.
Coordinates with the Senior Director of Program Operations to ensure Regional Directors and their teams are effectively connected to divisional training resources, program development support, and case management standards.
Supports Regional Directors in developing the competency and effectiveness of regional team members who matrix to program sites.
Schedules, as appropriate, in-service training, site visits, and professional development opportunities for regional social services personnel, in coordination with divisional functional leads.

People and Culture

Provides leadership, supervision, and development for the Regional Directors, and ensures regional team roles are staffed with individuals capable of delivering the mission effectively.
Ensures the regional team operates in an environment characterized by clear direction, effective communication, teamwork, and ongoing professional growth.
Fosters a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, and collaboration across the three regional teams and with divisional functional departments.
Acts as a representative of The Salvation Army and its mission in all internal and external relationships.

Other Duties

This job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive list of activities, duties, or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities and activities may change at any time with or without notice.

Minimum Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

Education

Master’s degree in social work, public administration, nonprofit management, human services, or a related field from an accredited institution is required.

Experience

Minimum of eight years of progressively responsible experience in social services leadership, program management, or human services administration, preferably in a multi-site nonprofit, faith-based, or human services environment.
Demonstrated experience serving in a senior leadership capacity, including acting on behalf of a senior executive or leading department-wide initiatives
Demonstrated experience leading and developing staff across multiple geographic regions or sites, including program oversight and service quality review.

Licenses/Certifications

Valid driver’s license and MVR clearance required for travel within the Division.
Caseworker Certification within 120 days of hire.

Skills/Abilities

Ability to lead across the full department and act with delegated authority on behalf of the Executive Director, exercising sound judgment on divisional matters.
Comprehensive understanding of social services field delivery, including community-based program operations, service coordination, and multi-site program management.
Working knowledge of The Salvation Army’s history, mission, and structure, as well as its services, policies, and procedures.
Demonstrated ability to develop and manage systems for regional service delivery, staff supervision, and program quality oversight.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to synthesize information from multiple regions and translate it into actionable direction.
Strong leadership, team building, and conflict management skills, including the ability to lead across geographic boundaries and complex matrix relationships.
Strong interpersonal and written communication skills, with the ability to engage effectively with diverse communities, site personnel, local stakeholders, and divisional colleagues.
Ability to manage multiple regions, priorities, and teams in a constantly changing environment.

JOB LIMITATIONS

This individual will adhere to all Salvation Army policies and procedures in carrying out the responsibilities of this position.

To successfully perform the essential functions of this position, the employee is regularly required to use standard office equipment and a PC. The work environment for this position is an office environment with a low to moderate noise level. Travel by car or air is required and occasionally outside the Division.

People. Pets. Community. 🐾

At the Cheyenne Animal Shelter (CAS), we believe that a healthy community honors every individual who calls it home—whether they walk on two legs or four. For over 50 years, we’ve been proudly serving Cheyenne and Laramie County as the largest community-centered animal resource center in Wyoming.

Our mission is to enhance the quality of life for animals and people through compassion, respect, and education. As proud practitioners of Socially Conscious Sheltering, we aren’t just a safe haven for displaced pets; we are an active hub of connection, safety, and support for the families who love them.

We are on a quest to establish CAS as the absolute best place to work in the community. To help us get there, we are looking for a warm, dynamic, and experienced leader to join our executive team as our Director of Operations.

The Opportunity: Position Summary

As our Director of Operations, you will hold the heart of our shelter’s daily operations in your hands. You will be responsible for executing the strategic direction and overall management of our core services—including Animal Care and Placement, Reunification, Facilities, Safety, and Post-Adoption Support (managed seamlessly through an advanced third-party integration platform).

This is an extraordinary opportunity to shape the future of our shelter. You will champion our internal culture, leading with a dedicated focus on steady performance, consistency, and a universally embraced standard of care. Additionally, because data transparency is central to our values, you will have the unique opportunity to build a brand-new reporting culture from the ground up—identifying key operational performance metrics and developing routine benchmarking systems.

You will directly supervise a passionate team (including our Shelter Manager, Animal Care Specialist, and Foster Care Specialist) and indirectly guide approximately 25 dedicated staff members in Animal and Customer Care.

Key Responsibilities Include

Financial Stewardship: Comfortably develop and manage a $2 million+ Shelter Operations budget, alongside our capital expense budget.
Community & Media Collaboration: Serve as an occasional public face of the shelter for media interviews, act as a vital community partner liaison, and join in the fun at our major fundraising events.
Strategic Partnerships: Act as our primary collaborator with outside government animal control entities and operational vendors.
Facilities & Safety: Act as the Shelter Safety Officer, ensuring our beautiful 21,000-square-foot facility, 9-acre grounds, and public dog park remain safe, clean, and OSHA-compliant.
Operational Support: Support your team by being ready to step in where needed—including obtaining your euthanasia certification within 90 days of hire.

Required

Experience: 5+ years of management experience, including direct employee supervision.
Education: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent applicable experience.
Skills: Strong computer literacy (Microsoft Office & Google Workspace), a high level of emotional intelligence, and a proven ability to gracefully navigate conflict and manage a healthy work/life balance.
Facilities Savvy: Basic competence in routine grounds and building maintenance management.
Requirements: Must be at least 21 years of age, hold a valid driver’s license, and be able to pass a background check and drug screen.

Demonstrated expertise in animal shelter operations and personnel management.
Master’s degree in Business, Public Administration, or a related field.
CAWA (Certified Animal Welfare Administrator) certification, or a desire to pursue it
Certifications in Lean Six Sigma, Project Management, or Organizational Leadership.
Familiarity with Fear-Free shelter philosophies and handling a variety of companion, exotic, or barnyard animals.

A starting salary of $75,000/year.
Excellent benefits, including medical, dental, and vision insurance.
Generous paid time off and flexible scheduling.
Dedicated, paid professional training funds to support your continuous personal and leadership development.
A workspace filled with passionate people, purpose, and plenty of tail wags.

Ready to Make an Impact?

If you are an intentional, data-minded, and compassionate leader who wants to go home every day knowing you made Cheyenne a more connected, resilient place for pets and people alike, we want to meet you!

State public health laboratories are foundational to protecting the health of the population. Only one of these highly specialized labs exist per state, creating a national network that works closely with the EPA, CDC, FDA and other federal agencies. The Colorado Public Health Laboratory (CPHL) protects the health of the population by identifying known and novel infectious diseases and outbreaks; detecting environmental contaminants in food products, natural medicine, and drinking and recreational waters; responding to bioterrorism and chemical threats; certifying every instrument in the state used for evidential breath alcohol testing; testing every infant born in Colorado and Wyoming to identify treatable genetic-related conditions at birth; performing audit functions and certification of outside laboratories; and conducting surveillance and public health research. The CPHL conducts around 3 million tests annually and works in partnership with local public health agencies to investigate and monitor public health threats.

The CPHL is a division with the Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment, known internally as the Laboratory Services Division. The Operations and Finance Unit of the laboratory delivers core operational, pre-analytical, and business support functions that enable timely, reliable, and compliant laboratory services. This unit integrates informatics and data systems, specimen accessioning, logistics and supply chain operations, client coordination, fiscal and contract management, and personnel administration into a cohesive operational framework that supports testing programs, regulatory requirements, and emergency response readiness. Through coordinated oversight of these interconnected functions, the unit ensures secure specimen and data flow, sound financial stewardship, effective workforce management, modern technology and instrumentation, and consistent customer service, allowing the laboratory’s scientific programs to operate efficiently while meeting public health priorities and surge demands.

This Operations and Finance unit also serves as the primary laboratory logistics partner to CDPHE’s Office of Emergency Preparedness and Response. The laboratory’s logistical support includes purchase, storage and distribution of vaccines, pharmaceuticals, personal protective equipment, and testing supplies; specimen transportation and testing support; and other logistical services necessary to support statewide preparedness, response, and recovery activities.

What You Will Do

Help lead one of Colorado’s most important public institutions.

Every day, the Colorado Public Health Laboratory protects millions of people by detecting infectious diseases, responding to outbreaks, identifying environmental contaminants, testing every newborn in Colorado and Wyoming for life-threatening conditions, supporting emergency response operations, and serving as a critical component of the nation’s public health infrastructure. More than three million tests flow through the laboratory each year.

We’re seeking an exceptional leader to serve as Deputy Director of Operations & Finance
, a senior executive role responsible for ensuring the laboratory has the people, systems, resources, technology, and operational excellence necessary to fulfill its mission.

This is not a traditional operations job.

You’ll oversee a complex portfolio that includes logistics, supply chain, specimen accessioning, laboratory informatics, fiscal operations, customer service, workforce administration, emergency and preparedness logistics. You’ll lead senior managers, shape organizational strategy, and serve as a trusted advisor to the Laboratory Director.

If you’re energized by solving complex problems, building high-performing teams, modernizing systems, and making a meaningful impact on public health, this may be the role you’ve been looking for.

Lead a Complex Public Health Enterprise

Provide executive leadership for the operational backbone of Colorado’s public health laboratory, ensuring secure, reliable, and compliant services that support critical testing programs and emergency response activities.

Build and Lead Exceptional Teams

Direct and mentor senior managers responsible for laboratory operations, logistics, fiscal services, client services, accessioning, and personnel administration. Shape workforce strategy, succession planning, and organizational development across multiple functional areas.

Drive Strategy and Operational Excellence

Strengthen Emergency Preparedness

Help lead one of Colorado’s critical emergency response assets. Oversee logistics and preparedness functions that support disease outbreak response, public health emergencies, medical countermeasure distribution, and statewide continuity of operations.

Shape the Future

Guide major initiatives involving technology modernization, laboratory informatics, facilities planning, organizational design, fiscal oversight, operational performance, and workforce readiness.

What Makes This Opportunity Unique

Lead operations for one of the most sophisticated public health laboratories in the nation.
Influence decisions that directly impact the health and safety of millions of Coloradans.

Manage a diverse portfolio that spans people, operations, finance, logistics, technology, and strategy.

Why This Work Matters

When a disease outbreak occurs, when drinking water is threatened, when a newborn needs a life-saving diagnosis, or when Colorado faces a public health emergency, the Colorado Public Health Laboratory is there.

new_jobs.description:
Job Description

We believe in bold ideas, diverse perspectives, and the drive to transform knowledge into impact. Here, your curiosity fuels progress, your voice shapes innovation, and your ambition helps redefine what’s possible within science and learning. We are a culture that obsesses over impact, challenges, and drives what’s next to power infinite possibilities for our customers, colleagues and society at large.

About The Role

The Chief of Staff to the CEO is one of the most consequential and demanding roles in the organization and one of the most distinct. This is not a traditional leadership role with a defined team, a clear mandate, or visible deliverables. It is a role built on influence without authority, on making others more effective rather than being visibly effective yourself, and on operating with the full trust of the CEO in a highly matrixed, fast-moving environment. The ideal candidate is a high-potential leader who is intellectually curious, politically astute, and genuinely energized by the challenge of working through others to drive outcomes that matter at the enterprise level.

Key Responsibilities

Coordination and Administration

Assist in managing the CEO’s agenda, ensuring focus on highest-priority areas.
Develop agendas for CEO-led meetings: ELT meetings, quarterly meetings, off-sites, etc. Work with CEO to identify key themes and topics and solicit input as needed from key stakeholders. Disseminate information to participants and coordinate follow-up.
Coordinate other CEO-led events and activities. Assist in developing content and agenda.
Coordinate board preparation; develop and disseminate materials; involve key stakeholders (among the ELT and others) as needed.
Ensure all materials shared with the CEO are synthesized, accurate, and current — always go to the source owners to verify information before distributing. Avoid relying on prior or undated materials.

Strategic Project Management

Lead and manage high-priority strategic initiatives on behalf of the CEO and executive leadership team, serving as project sponsor or direct project lead as appropriate.
Drive cross-functional strategic projects that span multiple business units, ensuring alignment with corporate objectives and timely delivery of outcomes.
Support the ELT in annual and multi-year strategic planning processes, including facilitating planning sessions, coordinating input from business units, and synthesizing strategic recommendations.
Identify and address critical organizational challenges that require CEO-level attention, developing action plans and mobilizing resources to drive resolution.
Track progress on enterprise-wide strategic initiatives; create executive dashboards and provide regular updates to the CEO and ELT on milestone achievements and risk mitigation.
Partner with business unit leaders to accelerate transformation initiatives, remove roadblocks, and ensure strategic alignment across the organization.
Conduct deep-dive analyses on strategic opportunities — including market entry, partnerships, M&A targets, or new business models — preparing executive-ready recommendations.
Serve as the CEO’s representative on select strategic workstreams, committees, or task forces, ensuring CEO priorities are reflected and progress is maintained.
A note on operating mode:
The Chief of Staff role is most powerful when it works – and wins – through others. Unlike a project owner with direct authority, this role operates through influence, facilitation, and relationship. The instinct to drive and own outcomes must be balanced with the discipline to let others lead — surfacing their thinking, giving them credit, and sequencing decisions so they land at the right moment, through the right voice.

Research

Coordinate background material and arrange briefings with CEO on important external meetings (investors, strategic hires, industry figures, etc.), working with Investor Relations, Business Heads, HR, and Corporate Communications.
Identify internal and external trends and events the CEO should be aware of, and prepare or coordinate background material as appropriate.
Ensure all information provided to the CEO is synthesized and summarized in a way that is accurate, reliable, and easy to consume — go directly to source owners to verify currency and correctness.

Relationship-Building

Maintain ongoing, positive relationships with all ELT members and other important stakeholders.
Ensure that the chief of staff role is apolitical — exercise judgment and discretion in disseminating information. Exercise confidentiality regarding privileged information.
Be seen as helpful and collaborative at all times; avoid assuming an unhelpful gatekeeper role.
Invest heavily in building relationship capital before it is needed. Early time spent in genuine, non-transactional engagement with ELT members pays dividends when influence is required later. Logic without relationship gets nowhere in a peer-influence environment.
Be explicit and disciplined about which mode you are operating in when engaging with senior executives: acting on the CEO’s behalf, offering your own perspective, or facilitating. Conflating these modes creates confusion and erodes trust.
Practice active listening as a core competency. When receiving feedback that differs from your perspective, pause, ask clarifying questions, and seek to understand before responding. Curiosity and openness are professional strengths in this role.

Advisory

Provide counsel to the CEO on critical business decisions and organizational challenges.
Feed organizational intelligence back to the CEO as appropriate.
Develop strong judgment about what to escalate vs. what to handle or redirect. Calibrate this explicitly and continuously with the CEO. Escalating too much reduces your value-add; escalating too little risks overstepping authority. Ask regularly: “Would you have wanted to know about X?”
Internalize that the “right” answer delivered at the wrong time, through the wrong messenger, or in the wrong room often produces a worse outcome than a less-optimal answer delivered well. Timing and sequencing are part of the answer.

What Success Looks Like In This Role

Many of the Chief of Staff’s most important contributions are invisible by design. A meeting that runs well because it was set up properly, a brewing conflict that dissolves before it reaches the CEO, a stalled decision that moves forward — these are the real deliverables. Success in this role is often measured by what didn’t happen, not by artifacts produced or decisions owned.

Indicators Of Strong Performance

Executives feel better prepared, aligned, and supported — and attribute that to themselves and their teams, not to the CoS.
The CEO’s time is protected and consistently applied to the highest-priority areas.
Information reaching the CEO is accurate, synthesized, and timely.
Cross-functional initiatives move forward without bottlenecks; the CoS is seen as a connector and enabler, not a checkpoint.
Trust with the ELT is high; the CoS is sought out, not worked around.

Qualifications

Ability to work closely with C-level executives; demonstrated professionalism, integrity, sense of urgency, discretion, and superior organizational skills.
Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment with appropriate technology fluency.
Outstanding communication skills, both written and verbal.
High emotional intelligence and ability to navigate sensitive situations with discretion.
Capacity to listen deeply and learn continuously — this role rewards pattern recognition developed through observation more than frameworks delivered through presentation.
Resilient and composed under pressure; able to stay grounded during an extended adjustment period (the transition into this role typically takes six to nine months before someone feels fully competent).
Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities with the ability to structure ambiguous problems and drive to actionable solutions.
Experience with project management methodologies and tools; ability to manage complex, multi-stakeholder initiatives.
Strategic thinking capability with the ability to connect tactical activities to broader organizational objectives.
Genuine commitment to professional networking — internally and externally — as a core working discipline, not an afterthought. Peer CoS relationships (within and outside the company) are a professional asset and a necessary sounding board for navigating this uniquely demanding role.

Additional Notes

The role requires flexibility, including occasional evening and weekend work. Some travel will be required.

For more than 200 years, we've transformed knowledge into discoveries that shape the world. Today, our global team of innovators, creators, and experts is driving what's next in science, education, and publishing—creating impact that reaches everywhere.

We're not just observers of progress. We're the ones accelerating scientific breakthroughs, advancing learning, and sparking innovation that redefines entire fields and improves lives.

NORTH & CENTRAL ILLINOIS DIVISION

Job Description

JOB TITLE:
Deputy Director of Social Services

Executive Director of Social Services

Exempt

413

Who We Are

At The Salvation Army, we are dedicated to “Doing the Most Good”. We are made up of thousands of officers, soldiers, staff, volunteers, donors, and partners working together to holistically meet the physical, emotional, and spiritual needs of our most vulnerable neighbors. We do this through programs designed to combat homelessness and hunger, provide safe spaces for kids after school and on the weekends, achieve and maintain sobriety, and give hope to the hopeless. The Salvation Army North and Central Illinois Division provides these services to people in need.

Job Summary

The Deputy Director of Social Services serves as the second-in-command of the Social Services Department, working in close partnership with the Executive Director of Social Services to provide divisional leadership, continuity, and accountability across the department. The Deputy Director helps advance department-wide strategy, planning, and priorities across all department capacities – Program Operations; Mission Investment Management; and Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning. In addition, the Deputy Director provides direct supervision to the three Regional Directors of Social Services serving Northwest Illinois, Central Illinois, and Chicago, ensuring consistent program oversight and site support across a large, geographically diverse Division by holding Regional Directors accountable for program quality, compliance, community engagement, and staff development within their regions.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Areas of responsibility include but are not limited to the following:

Divisional Deputy Leadership

Serves as second-in-command to the Executive Director of Social Services, acting on the Executive Director’s behalf and exercising delegated authority in their absence to ensure continuity of divisional leadership and decision-making.
Partners with the Executive Director on divisional strategy, planning, and department-wide priorities, and supports the setting of direction across all department capacities.
Represents the Executive Director and Social Services Department in internal and external settings as delegated, including with divisional leadership, funders, community partners, and committees.
Supports coordination and alignment across the divisional Senior Directors of Program Operations; Mission Investment Management; and Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning to advance shared department objectives.
Contributes to the development of departmental policies, procedures, and processes, and supports their consistent implementation across the department.

Regional Oversight and Divisional Authority

Provides oversight of social services delivery across the Division's three geographic regions – Northwest Illinois, Central Illinois, and Chicago – ensuring Regional Directors connect program sites to Program Operations support, Mission Investment Management, and Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning.
Provides direct supervision to the Regional Directors of Social Services, holding each accountable for the effectiveness of their regional team and the quality of support delivered to program sites.
Establishes and maintains the standards, expectations, and accountability structures that guide Regional Directors in delivering consistent, high-quality support across their regions.
Ensures clear role clarity across regional teams, resolving escalation questions as they arise and facilitating effective matrix relationships between Regional Directors and the divisional functional heads of Program Operations, Mission Investment Management, and Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning.
Coordinates with the Senior Directors of Program Operations, Mission Investment Management, and Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning to ensure regional counterparts are effectively connected to divisional resources, standards, and tools.
Anticipates and responds to changes in the regional operating environment and ensures Regional Directors are positioned to adapt their teams accordingly.

Impact Area Stewardship and Field Connectivity

Ensures Regional Directors serve as effective partners with site advisory boards, providing strategic guidance on program planning and community-responsive program development within their impact areas.
Ensures every active program site in each region has a clear and accessible regional point of contact for administrative support, program development, and capacity building.
Monitors the effectiveness of Regional Directors and their teams across all three geographic regions for consistency, responsiveness, and quality of site support.
Identifies patterns of field need across regions, ensures regional teams have what they need to support sites effectively, and escalates systemic issues to the Executive Director of Social Services.

Community Representation and Stakeholder Partnership

Ensures Regional Directors represent The Salvation Army effectively at regional and local levels, connecting program sites to community service agencies, social service providers, governmental agencies, and funding sources.
Supports Regional Directors in building and sustaining local stakeholder relationships that advance mission outcomes and increase community visibility for program sites.
Coordinates with corps officers, program and related institution directors, and local advisory boards, through Regional Directors, to advance program development that is grounded in community need and aligned with divisional priorities.
Represents The Salvation Army on regional and local committees, task forces, and community planning bodies, as assigned.
Cooperates with other social service agencies in community planning, needs assessments, information and referral, and case management coordination, as appropriate.

Regional Program Oversight Coordination

Oversee Regional Directors’ work to ensure program sites within each region maintain compliance with licensing, accreditation, and Salvation Army standards.
Coordinates with the Senior Director of Mission Investment Management to ensure compliance support reaches program sites effectively through the matrix.
Supports Regional Directors in conducting periodic program reviews that assess service quality, fiscal alignment, and consistency with divisional priorities.
Coordinates with the Senior Director of Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning to ensure outcome tools and performance tracking support reaches program sites effectively through the matrix.
Ensures that program development proposals or modifications at the regional and site level reflect community need, divisional strategic priorities, and organizational capacity before advancing to the Executive Director.

Capacity Building and Staff Development

Builds the leadership capacity of Regional Directors through direct supervision, mentorship, and ongoing professional development, ensuring each director has the skills to lead their regional team effectively.
Ensures Regional Directors equip their site-level teams with the knowledge, tools, and practical support needed to deliver programs effectively.
Coordinates with the Senior Director of Program Operations to ensure Regional Directors and their teams are effectively connected to divisional training resources, program development support, and case management standards.
Supports Regional Directors in developing the competency and effectiveness of regional team members who matrix to program sites.
Schedules, as appropriate, in-service training, site visits, and professional development opportunities for regional social services personnel, in coordination with divisional functional leads.

People and Culture

Provides leadership, supervision, and development for the Regional Directors, and ensures regional team roles are staffed with individuals capable of delivering the mission effectively.
Ensures the regional team operates in an environment characterized by clear direction, effective communication, teamwork, and ongoing professional growth.
Fosters a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, and collaboration across the three regional teams and with divisional functional departments.
Acts as a representative of The Salvation Army and its mission in all internal and external relationships.

Other Duties

This job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive list of activities, duties, or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities and activities may change at any time with or without notice.

Minimum Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

Education

Master’s degree in social work, public administration, nonprofit management, human services, or a related field from an accredited institution is required.

Experience

Minimum of eight years of progressively responsible experience in social services leadership, program management, or human services administration, preferably in a multi-site nonprofit, faith-based, or human services environment.
Demonstrated experience serving in a senior leadership capacity, including acting on behalf of a senior executive or leading department-wide initiatives
Demonstrated experience leading and developing staff across multiple geographic regions or sites, including program oversight and service quality review.

Licenses/Certifications

Valid driver’s license and MVR clearance required for travel within the Division.
Caseworker Certification within 120 days of hire.

Skills/Abilities

Ability to lead across the full department and act with delegated authority on behalf of the Executive Director, exercising sound judgment on divisional matters.
Comprehensive understanding of social services field delivery, including community-based program operations, service coordination, and multi-site program management.
Working knowledge of The Salvation Army’s history, mission, and structure, as well as its services, policies, and procedures.
Demonstrated ability to develop and manage systems for regional service delivery, staff supervision, and program quality oversight.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to synthesize information from multiple regions and translate it into actionable direction.
Strong leadership, team building, and conflict management skills, including the ability to lead across geographic boundaries and complex matrix relationships.
Strong interpersonal and written communication skills, with the ability to engage effectively with diverse communities, site personnel, local stakeholders, and divisional colleagues.
Ability to manage multiple regions, priorities, and teams in a constantly changing environment.

People. Pets. Community. 🐾

At the Cheyenne Animal Shelter (CAS), we believe that a healthy community honors every individual who calls it home—whether they walk on two legs or four. For over 50 years, we’ve been proudly serving Cheyenne and Laramie County as the largest community-centered animal resource center in Wyoming.

Our mission is to enhance the quality of life for animals and people through compassion, respect, and education. As proud practitioners of Socially Conscious Sheltering, we aren’t just a safe haven for displaced pets; we are an active hub of connection, safety, and support for the families who love them.

You will be responsible for executing the strategic direction and overall management of our core services—including Animal Care and Placement, Reunification, Facilities, Safety, and Post-Adoption Support (managed seamlessly through an advanced third-party integration platform).

This is an extraordinary opportunity to shape the future of our shelter. You will champion our internal culture, leading with a dedicated focus on steady performance, consistency, and a universally embraced standard of care. Additionally, because data transparency is central to our values, you will have the unique opportunity to build a brand-new reporting culture from the ground up—identifying key operational performance metrics and developing routine benchmarking systems.

You will directly supervise a passionate team (including our Shelter Manager, Animal Care Specialist, and Foster Care Specialist) and indirectly guide approximately 25 dedicated staff members in Animal and Customer Care.

Financial Stewardship: Comfortably develop and manage a $2 million+ Shelter Operations budget, alongside our capital expense budget.
Community & Media Collaboration: Serve as an occasional public face of the shelter for media interviews, act as a vital community partner liaison, and join in the fun at our major fundraising events.
Strategic Partnerships: Act as our primary collaborator with outside government animal control entities and operational vendors.
Facilities & Safety: Act as the Shelter Safety Officer, ensuring our beautiful 21,000-square-foot facility, 9-acre grounds, and public dog park remain safe, clean, and OSHA-compliant.

Required

Experience: 5+ years of management experience, including direct employee supervision.

Skills: Strong computer literacy (Microsoft Office & Google Workspace), a high level of emotional intelligence, and a proven ability to gracefully navigate conflict and manage a healthy work/life balance.

Requirements: Must be at least 21 years of age, hold a valid driver’s license, and be able to pass a background check and drug screen.

Master’s degree in Business, Public Administration, or a related field.
CAWA (Certified Animal Welfare Administrator) certification, or a desire to pursue it
Certifications in Lean Six Sigma, Project Management, or Organizational Leadership.
Familiarity with Fear-Free shelter philosophies and handling a variety of companion, exotic, or barnyard animals.

A starting salary of $75,000/year.
Excellent benefits, including medical, dental, and vision insurance.
Generous paid time off and flexible scheduling.
Dedicated, paid professional training funds to support your continuous personal and leadership development.
A workspace filled with passionate people, purpose, and plenty of tail wags.

If you are an intentional, data-minded, and compassionate leader who wants to go home every day knowing you made Cheyenne a more connected, resilient place for pets and people alike, we want to meet you!

Description Of Job

The Work Unit:

State public health laboratories are foundational to protecting the health of the population. Only one of these highly specialized labs exist per state, creating a national network that works closely with the EPA, CDC, FDA and other federal agencies. The Colorado Public Health Laboratory (CPHL) protects the health of the population by identifying known and novel infectious diseases and outbreaks; detecting environmental contaminants in food products, natural medicine, and drinking and recreational waters; responding to bioterrorism and chemical threats; certifying every instrument in the state used for evidential breath alcohol testing; testing every infant born in Colorado and Wyoming to identify treatable genetic-related conditions at birth; performing audit functions and certification of outside laboratories; and conducting surveillance and public health research. The CPHL conducts around 3 million tests annually and works in partnership with local public health agencies to investigate and monitor public health threats.

The CPHL is a division with the Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment, known internally as the Laboratory Services Division. The Operations and Finance Unit of the laboratory delivers core operational, pre-analytical, and business support functions that enable timely, reliable, and compliant laboratory services. This unit integrates informatics and data systems, specimen accessioning, logistics and supply chain operations, client coordination, fiscal and contract management, and personnel administration into a cohesive operational framework that supports testing programs, regulatory requirements, and emergency response readiness. Through coordinated oversight of these interconnected functions, the unit ensures secure specimen and data flow, sound financial stewardship, effective workforce management, modern technology and instrumentation, and consistent customer service, allowing the laboratory’s scientific programs to operate efficiently while meeting public health priorities and surge demands.

This Operations and Finance unit also serves as the primary laboratory logistics partner to CDPHE’s Office of Emergency Preparedness and Response. Help lead one of Colorado’s most important public institutions.

You’ll lead senior managers, shape organizational strategy, and serve as a trusted advisor to the Laboratory Director.

If you’re energized by solving complex problems, building high-performing teams, modernizing systems, and making a meaningful impact on public health, this may be the role you’ve been looking for.

Lead a Complex Public Health Enterprise

Provide executive leadership for the operational backbone of Colorado’s public health laboratory, ensuring secure, reliable, and compliant services that support critical testing programs and emergency response activities.

Build and Lead Exceptional Teams

Shape the Future

Influence decisions that directly impact the health and safety of millions of Coloradans.

Why This Work Matters

When a disease outbreak occurs, when drinking water is threatened, when a newborn needs a life-saving diagnosis, or when Colorado faces a public health emergency, the Colorado Public Health Laboratory is there.
